name: ransom_note_scan
description: Find files whose names look like ransom notes (a name match is a CANDIDATE, not a note) and locate what is in them without printing it. Each candidate is read once (up to max_size, 16 MiB at most), decoded by byte-order mark, then by the NUL pattern of UTF-16 without one, else UTF-8 (decoding errors counted; a binary file is listed and not read as text), and classified `content_resembles_note` when its content shows at least two kinds of note marker (an onion address, a wallet, a Tox id, a labelled identifier, note vocabulary) and otherwise `filename_only`; neither confirms a note. Indicator candidates are found by pattern: onion addresses, e-mail addresses, URLs, bitcoin, monero and ethereum addresses, Tox ids and the value after a label such as "your personal ID" (kind identifier_candidate); a bitcoin address's own checksum is checked (checksum_valid, checksum_failed) and the rest are syntactic candidates, none attributed to anyone. The answer is a locator: per note its id, size, sha256 of the whole file (withheld, with the reason, for a note shorter than 128 bytes or one that is a single token or indicator value, where it would be a digest of the value), modification time (raw nanoseconds and ISO UTC, as collected), class, encoding, decoding errors and a count per kind; per occurrence its finding id, byte offset, length and validation. No identifier, wallet, address, URL, key or note text is in the answer or in any file it names, and any path component that holds an identifier-shaped token (a run of 8 or more letters and digits holding both, a run of 10 or more digits, a run of 8 or more letters that is not one word, a capitalised word, several capitalised words or all capitals, a run of 16 or more letters of one case, 8 or more pairs of hex digits joined by one character that is not a letter, a digit or a slash (a colon, a dash, a dot, an underscore, a space, a bracket; a neighbour of the run that is not a letter or a digit does not hide it, a letter or a digit glued to a pair makes that pair no pair), or groups of three or more digits joined by a space or a comma that hold 10 digits or more; a name is folded first: full-width forms, digits of any script, a full-width solidus as a separator, and no invisible character: format characters, combining marks, variation selectors, fillers), a token, key or user-info the shared withholding rules find, or a value the note held, is withheld from every path it prints (notes, rejected name matches, directories it could not list, exclusions, the root) and counted once per printed path in paths_withheld. A name that is withheld is replaced by one constant marker, so that nothing derived from it is printed: no length, no extension, no stem, and the place of the name among its siblings does not follow its text either (names that print alike, the withheld ones, come in an order drawn afresh every run, so a row, a note id, a finding id and the files a limit keeps are in that order, which differs between runs); the order of names that print alike is a keyed hash of the whole path, so the same name under two directories has two unrelated ranks. A name the first rule lets through but that is withheld because the note beneath it holds its value sorts as a withheld name too: the notes are read in a first pass (at most 40% of max_seconds; `first_pass` says whether it finished, and when it did not, every name of 8 characters or more sorts as a withheld one) before the walk that prints is ordered, so a note whose path holds a name of 8 characters or more is read a second time, and matched a second time only when it holds a piece of such a name (8 characters of it), and a note is matched for onion addresses, e-mail addresses and ethereum addresses only when it holds the literal such a match must hold (`.onion`, `@`, `0x`): six 12 MiB notes with no match took 11.4 CPU s with no first pass, 21.6 with a first pass that matched every note and 7.4 with this one; 50,000 files with a note in a fifth of the directories, small notes: 1.3, 2.1 and 1.6 to 2.0 CPU s). A name withheld in the rows of some notes and printed in others sorts with the withheld names, and a note that changed between the two passes is ordered by what the first pass read. A second check, written apart from the rule, reads every string of the answer, of every page and of the census on its way out and replaces one that is still identifier-shaped by a marker, makes a complete answer partial and says where in `boundary`; the one thing it lets through is the name of an ordinary file, which is evidence. A size of 10 or more digits followed by `bytes` in the tool's own sentences (a reason, a status basis) is a number, not an identifier, and the type of an error (IsADirectoryError) is a word. Names of well-known directories (System32, SysWOW64, INetCache, INetCookies, INetHistory, MSOCache, PSReadLine, Framework, Framework64, SQLServer, GPUCache, DawnWebGPUCache, DawnGraphiteCache, GrShaderCache, IndexedDB, overlay2, datastore1) are printed in any case. The identifier shape is a guess and its rates were measured on random draws per shape as a directory name (5,000 for the first rule, 1,000 for the later classes). Printed whole (100%): a token of seven characters or fewer, 8 or 9 decimal digits, groups of four joined by a dash, an underscore or a dot, two groups of 7 letters joined by a dash, up to 15 letters of one case (8 to 15 lower-case letters, 8 to 15 capitals), and a mix of Cyrillic look-alike letters and digits (99.9%); 7 pairs of hex digits joined by a colon, a dot or a space 100% (by a dash 29%), three groups of 3, 3 and 4 digits joined by a dash 100%, and 8 pairs of hex digits with a letter or a digit glued to a pair at an end of the run (the run then counts a pair fewer) 100% when the pairs are joined by a colon, a space or a dot (by a dash 3 to 15%). Printed some of the time: a random 8-character letters-and-digits token 3.3% (9 characters 2.2%, 12 characters 0.6%, 16 characters 0.1%), 8 lower-case letters and digits 7.1%, 12 full-width letters and digits 0.7%, and mixed-case letters (40,000 draws each) 12 characters 5.8%, 16 characters 2.4%, 24 characters 0.5%. Not printed (0 of 1,000): hex of 16, 32 or 64 characters, 12 or 20 decimal digits, 12 digits of another script, a UUID, base58 of 22 characters, base32 of 16 characters, 16 or more letters of one case, hex, 12 digits and 12 letters-and-digits split by invisible characters (format characters, combining marks, variation selectors, fillers: 0 of 7,875 each, in the middle and at an end), 8 pairs of hex digits joined by a colon, a dash, a dot or a space (also inside brackets, after an equals sign or in parentheses: id[aa-bb-...], key=aa:bb:...), and three groups of four digits joined by a space or a comma. The 16-letter rule has a cost: on 1,314,483 real directory components of another developer machine (150,000 directories) the rule withheld 5.5% of the components and some component of 40.0% of the directories before it and 5.8% and 41.8% with it (appletvsimulator and managedapplications are withheld with the 32-letter Chrome extension ids it is meant to catch). On a developer machine's application, cache and package trees the rule before it withheld 4.9% of 600,000 real directory components (dates, versions and package ids hold digits among letters) and some component of 38% of their directories, so a harmless name is often withheld: list the directory for it. Names are judged by shape only, by a deny-list of shapes that is not finite: an identifier of another shape is printed, and a new shape found is one more that was. Printed whole too (100% of 1,000 draws each unless a rate is given, as a directory name and as a file name; measured with the scan's copy of the rule, which a test holds equal to the survey's): 8 or more pairs of hex digits joined by a separator of two characters or more (a comma and a space, two colons, a dash with a space on each side, `][`, `)(`, `0xAA,0xBB`, every pair in brackets; two dashes 19%); 7 pairs joined by a no-break or an ideographic space or a comma (by an underscore or a percent sign 28 to 29%); a 6-pair MAC address with colons or dashes, a Cisco one (aabb.ccdd.eeff), an IPv6 address; digits in other groupings: 3, 3 and 4 joined by a dot, an underscore or an apostrophe, 1.234.567.890.123, two groups of 6 digits or 12 single digits joined by a dot, a dash, an underscore or an apostrophe, pairs of digits joined by a space or a comma; 5 groups of 5 or 3 groups of 7 letters or digits joined by a space, 4 groups of 6 joined by a dot, three groups of 7 letters joined by a dash, base32 in groups of 4 joined by a space, two 7-digit hex tokens joined by a dot or a dash; 16 CJK ideographs, emoji, a mix of Greek look-alike letters (99%), words joined by a dash; eight two-digit-hex directories one under another, and 4 pairs in a directory with 4 in the file name (a run of pairs is read within one path component). The second check reads the same shapes, so it holds the same classes. SENSITIVE: a note can hold access tokens. write_values: true (refused outside a job, and in a job whose process lacks SECRET_OUTPUT=1; the manifest makes every job that sets write_values secret output) creates $OUT/ransom-note-values.jsonl, mode 0600, before it scans (a file or link already there is refused by name) and writes the values, a preview of each note's first lines and the real paths to it and nowhere else. It follows no link and reads only regular files; every name match it did not read (a link, a special file, empty, over max_size, unreadable) is listed with the reason, and `status` (also `complete`) says `partial`, with `status_basis`, when one could have held something or the time limit (max_seconds, default 480, below the manifest's 600) stopped the walk or a note, naming how many entries and directories were not examined; the clock runs inside a note too (reading, then matching every pattern, the URL and identifier patterns too, looked at between pieces of 256 KiB of text, so a note with no match at all is cut as well), and a note it cut is counted in notes_partly_scanned and carries scan_stopped. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer (status failed, interrupted, exit code 128 + the signal) after removing the pages it was writing; a values file already begun is kept, cut back to its last whole row, and the answer says how many rows it holds. A page file already there is never replaced: the new one takes the next free name, and the answer names it. The earliest note time is an observation of the filesystem's mtime as collected, not the start of the run. A note named otherwise, an image of a note, an encoding it does not detect and a long unlabelled token (no label, no known shape: a 64-digit hex string after the word "Token") are not found, not located and not counted. Takes a directory tree, so it has no `use` triggers. SIGKILL cannot be caught: a tool killed that way (the job service's last resort after its grace period) leaves the hidden temporary files of the census and the pages in tool-output, named by no answer and holding only rows already read back by the second check, and, in a window of microseconds, an empty file at a result name; delete them. The job's own timeout_seconds (default 900 for the survey, 600 for the scan) is not passed to the tool: give max_seconds a value below it, because a job stopped by its timeout answers failed, not partial.

root.description: A directory to sweep (an extracted tree, not an image)

max_size.description: Largest file to read as a note (default 200000, at least 16, at most 16777216); a name match above it is listed as not read, with its size

limit.description: Rows shown inline per table (default 100); every row is counted, and a table with more is written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages.<table>.all_results

write_values.description: Write each value found, and a preview of each note, to $OUT/ransom-note-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job run as secret output (the manifest makes a job that sets this one; the tool checks SECRET_OUTPUT=1 in its environment); the file is created first and a file or link already there is refused; the answer never carries a value

exclude_top_level_dirs.description: Directory names skipped at the top of the root only (default ["proc", "sys", "dev"]); each is listed as an exclusion. [] excludes nothing; a directory of that name deeper in the tree is always read

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 480, at most 540; the manifest's timeout is 600). When it runs out the walk stops, what was read is written, and the answer is partial and says how many entries and directories were not examined. The clock runs inside a note too: reading and matching stop at the limit and the note is reported as partly scanned
